raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Underwriting perspective on AI CapEx cycle, risk assessment, and potential job losses due to AI efficiency",
  "main_topics": [
    "AI CapEx cycle",
    "Underwriting perspective",
    "Risk assessment",
    "Job losses due to AI efficiency"
  ],
  "answer_completeness": "Partial",
  "response_stance": "Hedged",
  "evidence_level": "Medium",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": false,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Partially aligned",
  "question_quote": "My questions are more on the AI sort of CapEx cycle and if you could help us think through it. So, some of the plans in the US of the hyperscalers have humongous sort of numbers behind on the CapEx side, which, I mean, it looks good for business, issuance, etc, presumably deal logic suggests that year-to-date, things are going very, very well. But on the other side, we see a lot of the banks offloading data centre risk and some of these numbers, the share price reaction questioning if it's a good use of money. How are you thinking about it from an underwriting perspective? Are you just intermediating, issuing, helping them issuing the bonds? Or how much risk are you taking from a credit perspective? Or how are you thinking about it? And potentially on the other side, more as you think further down the line as well on the underwriting risk, how do you think about AI affecting the underwriting risk more broadly? I'm thinking also here on the retail side, the risk of disruption sort of efficiencies and ultimately would lead to job losses. Can you help us think through it because that's also doing the round.",
  "answer_quote": "So let me start with sort of AI / software just as an Investment Bank matter. I mean we don't think of this as differently to other sectors really. So, expect us - and I think it's Slide 100 in the deck, expect us to deal with this type of credit with the same degree of rigor, even though it's had clearly a huge strategic focus, there is a massive sort of build in funding in the US. From our perspective, we would maintain the same kind of concentration limits, the same kind of sector diversification requirements as we would have anywhere else, both in terms of the sector and the counterparties involved. Expect us to deal with parties that are relatively larger and more established, etc. So, just a continuation of that really. If we had significant concentrations, you would see it in our disclosures, and you can see that actually it's subsumed within a much larger bucket, the name which I've completely forgotten, but we will come back to you. So it's not an outsized position for us. That said, given the activities over the last sort of four to six weeks, we are extremely focused on it and extremely focused on the levels of risk. And obviously, here, we use SRT as we use elsewhere in other sectors. So, nothing to call out if there were, then we would have done so. In terms of underwriting on personal, we've had some really interesting questions on the road on this actually as to whether or not we should be expecting more of a white-collar recession versus a blue-collar recession, particularly in the US. But we see no movement in credit thus far. We're obviously very watchful as we always are, both in the UK and in the US. It feels a bit early to call the shape of the impact from many of our competitors and many firms across the industry, they're not really talking about headcount reduction. They're really talking about the spending that they're undertaking and perhaps technology efficiency. So, we will watch it very, very carefully. We're also very mindful that AI and sort of data more generally can bring us huge benefits on the underwriting side just because of our ability to ingest data and process that data. That's actually the fundamental basis of Best Egg. So, we do see opportunities to learn here. I think it's on both sides of that particular argument, Alvaro, but very, very watchful.",
  "reason": "The answer provides a hedged perspective on the AI CapEx cycle, discussing underwriting practices and risk assessment without directly addressing the question's concern about job losses due to AI efficiency, thus only partially completing the question's intent."
}
